messages:
Alex P: Hey — publishing pipeline started failing intermittently for the infra builder images. GitOps promote is blocked because the manifest list we push doesn't have an SBOM for linux/arm64 (CI only shows amd64). snippet from the publish job log:
```
2026-03-17T15:04:12Z publish: pushing manifest list -> ok
2026-03-17T15:04:13Z verify: SBOM missing for platform linux/arm64 -> error: validation failed
```
Anyone else seeing this? :eyes:

buildbot: [CI] publish-builder #432 failed — missing platform SBOM (linux/arm64). job: ci/publish-builder/432, runner: build-runner-us-west-2-7

Michelle L: Which job specifically? is that the multi-arch buildx step or a separate sbom task? Can you paste the full job name so I can re-run locally?

Alex P: It's the multi-arch pipeline: .github/workflows/publish-builder.yml -> job: build-and-publish (runs on build-runner-us-west-2). Repro attempt fails on my laptop when I only emulate arm64 locally, but succeeds on amd64.

Jorge R: My hunch: builder-runner in us-west-2 is using an older skopeo/umoci version that doesn't attach the generated SBOM blob to the arm64 manifest entry. We've hit something like this before when buildx delegates to remote builders with mismatched tool versions. To reproduce/verify locally run:
```
# build and push multi-arch (example)
docker buildx create --use --name redwood-builder || true
docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64 -t registry.redwood.dev/infra/builder-base:pr-432 --push .
# inspect manifest platforms/digests
skopeo inspect --raw docker://registry.redwood.dev/infra/builder-base:pr-432 | jq '.manifests[] | {platform:.platform, digest:.digest}'
# validate sbom presence per-platform (example check)
./scripts/verify-sbom.sh registry.redwood.dev/infra/builder-base:pr-432 linux/arm64
```
Also cosign signing sometimes gets skipped on a per-arch job if the runner loses state — ensure cosign runs after manifests are assembled, not per-platform before the manifest push.

Tanya S: Proposal: add explicit per-platform SBOM generation step (spdx/syft) and a gate that fails if any platform lacks an sbom blob or signature. We can add a quick skopeo/jq gate in CI that extracts manifests and checks for an SBOM artifact reference or label. Example snippet to fail CI if no sbom:
```
MANIFESTS=$(skopeo inspect --raw docker://$IMAGE | jq -c '.manifests[]')
for m in $MANIFESTS; do
  digest=$(echo $m | jq -r '.digest')
  # check if SBOM exists in the registry under /sbom/<digest>.spdx.json or similar
  curl -sfL $REGISTRY/v2/$REPO/blobs/sha256:${digest_sans_alg}.sbom || exit 1
done
```
I'll add a small GH Actions job that runs in parallel to the buildx push and runs the verification script.

Rupert: FYI region note — our busiest ARM runners are in us-west-2 (GPU fleet churn + spot eviction policies pushed some infra runners into high load). Could be flakiness from I/O or registry throttling as well. If runners lose ephemeral state mid-push, manifest assembly can miss auxiliary blobs. Two mitigation ideas: 1) temporarily route builder jobs to eu-west-1 where runners are less contended, 2) pin the base image digest in Helm charts so rolling updates don't rely on manifest re-resolution during promote. Both are low-effort.

Michelle L: I'll open a PR to: (a) add the sbom+signature gate job, (b) move cosign signing to manifest-level step, (c) add skopeo manifest/digest assertions. I'll also include a fallback that re-tries manifest push once on 5xx/transport errors.

Alex P: Thanks — can you also include a small Terraform tweak to bump builder-runner autoscaling min size by +1 in us-west-2 while we test? that should reduce immediate contention. Keep the change minimal and feature-flagged.

Michelle L: Yep — will do a combined infra + pipeline PR and link the issue.

buildbot: [CI] re-run scheduled: ci/publish-builder/432 -> triggered by @Michelle L

Alex P: Awesome, thanks team :thumbsup:
